subject: Re: New pilot study
body:
Hi Sara, Petra, (Sandra (PI on the project)),

Thanks for reaching out.

We don’t have an ID ourselves yet, perhaps @Petra Olsthoorn has one? Otherwise, any generated ID will do.

Here is a short description/abstract of the eventual full study: Street-level-bureaucrats (SLBs) need to be responsive to individual demands and needs of citizens during citizen-state interaction in order to provide adequate public services. In these cases, street-level-bureaucrats have to provide user-centered services, taking into account citizen’s specific situations, demands and needs. How SLBs can user-centered public services and what prerequisite knowledge, skills, competencies and conditions are required to effectively do so, remains fairly unknown. This research aims to explore the experiences and interactions of SLBs during processes of public service delivery, thereby filling the gap in our knowledge on how SLBs can provide user-centered public services and what prerequisite skills, competencies and conditions are required to effectively do so.

Therefore, the goal of this explorative study is to track SLBs’ diary reports on their day-to-day experiences and provide a comprehensive oversight of the prerequisites for user-centered public service provision. To do so, longitudinal qualitative data (brief “stories” and responses) are collected by means of a digital diary study, whereby approximately 60 SLBs working in approximately 5 diverse government organizations fill out a diary featuring approximately 18 questions about their day-to-day experiences in providing (user-centered) public services to citizens every week for a period of 10 weeks. Based on thematic analysis of these data (responses, stories of max 100-150 words), we aim to answer the research question: “What are required knowledge and competencies for user-centered public services provision in day-to-day citizens-state interactions, according to the perspective of individual SLBs?”.

In addition two remaining questions:

  • Do you have any experience with the application not working in case of certain cellphones with security layers, i.e. government cell phones from regular public servants
  • For the pilot study, we want to test the application and the questionnaire and see whether it works well. Initially, I was thinking about running the pilot only myself as a respondent (hence 1 respondent in the request) but it might also be useful to have another pilot respondent who actually is a SLB (to gather practitioner feedback + check whether the app works in case of government cellphones that may have certain security layers). Is that possible?

Met vriendelijke groet/Kind regards,

Dr. Glenn Houtgraaf | Post-Doctoral Researcher

subject: New pilot study
body:
Hi Glenn,

Thank you for sharing the detailed description of your study. It sounds like a fascinating research project and we would be more than happy to be part of it.

Regarding the study ID, we are referring to the ID of your study when you create it on your researcher dashboard in Avicenna. You can easily find it on your study's "Basics" page. More on this here.

To address your remaining questions:
  • Compatibility with Government Cell Phones: I don’t remember any instances where we faced compatibility issues with government cell phones. I recommend testing the application on different devices to identify any potential issues early. If you face specific problems, please don’t hesitate to reach out, and we can help resolve them.
  • Pilot Study Setup: It is certainly possible to include additional pilot respondents who are SLBs if needed. This approach could be very helpful in ensuring the app's functionality and usability, especially in environments with stricter security measures. Please let me know if I can assist with setting this up for a smooth testing phase.
If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to contact me.

Best,
Sara

subject: New pilot study
body:
Hi Glenn,

I hope you are doing well. I'm glad to hear that you have had a good experience with Avicenna so far.

Thank you for reaching out with your question. At the moment, we do not have the option to put more than one question on a page. Our experience has shown that presenting one question per page has led to higher user engagement and improved user experiences, ultimately increasing the likelihood of receiving responses from users. However, we understand that you may prefer to have this option, and we have already planned this feature in our roadmap. If this is critical for your study, please let me know.

If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

Best,
Sara

Hi Sara, Petra, (Sandra (PI on the project)),

Thanks for reaching out.

We don’t have an ID ourselves yet, perhaps @Petra Olsthoorn has one? Otherwise, any generated ID will do.

Here is a short description/abstract of the eventual full study: Street-level-bureaucrats (SLBs) need to be responsive to individual demands and needs of citizens during citizen-state interaction in order to provide adequate public services. In these cases, street-level-bureaucrats have to provide user-centered services, taking into account citizen’s specific situations, demands and needs. How SLBs can user-centered public services and what prerequisite knowledge, skills, competencies and conditions are required to effectively do so, remains fairly unknown. This research aims to explore the experiences and interactions of SLBs during processes of public service delivery, thereby filling the gap in our knowledge on how SLBs can provide user-centered public services and what prerequisite skills, competencies and conditions are required to effectively do so.

Therefore, the goal of this explorative study is to track SLBs’ diary reports on their day-to-day experiences and provide a comprehensive oversight of the prerequisites for user-centered public service provision. To do so, longitudinal qualitative data (brief “stories” and responses) are collected by means of a digital diary study, whereby approximately 60 SLBs working in approximately 5 diverse government organizations fill out a diary featuring approximately 18 questions about their day-to-day experiences in providing (user-centered) public services to citizens every week for a period of 10 weeks. Based on thematic analysis of these data (responses, stories of max 100-150 words), we aim to answer the research question: “What are required knowledge and competencies for user-centered public services provision in day-to-day citizens-state interactions, according to the perspective of individual SLBs?”.

In addition two remaining questions:

  • Do you have any experience with the application not working in case of certain cellphones with security layers, i.e. government cell phones from regular public servants
  • For the pilot study, we want to test the application and the questionnaire and see whether it works well.
